frozen_original.synopsis: White House deletes Spanish website and social media accounts. Around approximately 4 p.m. Eastern, just hours after Donald Trump's inauguration, the Spanish versions of the White House website and social media accounts were removed from the internet. This post will be updated if any additional context becomes available. proposal.description_long: Within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration, the White House Spanish-language homepage became unavailable and showed an error page. The Associated Press reported the change the next day and identified @LaCasaBlanca, the White House’s Spanish-language X profile, and a government reproductive-freedom page as also disbanded. When asked about the changes, White House principal deputy press secretary Harrison Fields said the administration was developing and editing the website, that some archived content had gone dormant, and that it was committed to bringing the Spanish translation section back online. AP also noted that Trump had removed a Spanish White House page in 2017 and that the Biden administration restored it in 2021. These details distinguish the observed outage and account removals from an established permanent shutdown: the administration described the website status as transition work and promised restoration, though the report did not specify a date. The corrected entry should say the services went offline during the transition and include the administration’s stated explanation. It should not claim all Spanish-language government accounts were permanently deleted.
proposal.description_medium: The Associated Press reported that the new administration took down the White House Spanish-language website within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration; the Spanish-language X profile @LaCasaBlanca and a reproductive-freedom page were also disbanded. A White House spokesperson said the site was being edited and that archived content had gone dormant, and said the translation section would return. The evidence supports unavailability during the transition, not a permanent deletion claim.
